about-hero-subtitle: Society of Montfort Brothers of St. Gabriel
about-statement1-text: Montfortian Education is committed to the Gospel values of Equality, fraternity, freedom and human brotherhood, striving to transform the society through the education mission, for the establishment of the reign of God.
about-statement2-text: We, the Montfort Brothers of St. Gabriel together with all our associates, by our value based educational endeavors hope to build a fraternal society by molding the personality of each individual under our care, trusting in God and drawing inspiration from our Founder St. Louis Marie De Montfort
about-statement3-text: We shall strive to make socially conscious and concerned individuals who reach the destined level of excellence and take up the responsibility as leaders of integrity with a preferential option for the less privileged.
about-heritage-p1: Born on 31 January 1673, Louis-Marie Grignion—affectionately known as Montfort—emerged as a prophetic voice of his time. He recognized the presence of God in the poor and dedicated his entire life to their upliftment. From within him flowed an unfailing stream of love, courage, selfless service, and deep commitment to the marginalized and the downtrodden. At the heart of this inexhaustible zeal was his guiding motto:
about-heritage-p2: Montfort entered eternal life on 28 April 1716, yet his spirit continues to inspire the world today through the three congregations he founded—the Montfort Brothers of St. Gabriel, the Priests of the Company of Mary (Montfort Fathers), and the Daughters of Wisdom—as well as through numerous Montfortian Associates who keep his mission alive.

about-congregation-title: The Montfort Brothers of St. Gabriel
about-cong-p1: The Congregation of the Montfort Brothers of St. Gabriel forms a vibrant religious community within the Catholic Church. Founded by St. Louis-Marie de Montfort, the Brothers are consecrated religious inspired by Jesus Christ. They profess the vows of poverty, chastity, and obedience, choosing to live in communities where everything is shared and no member claims anything as his own.
about-edu-p1: Education remains one of the congregation’s primary ministries, with a special focus on children and youth—particularly those from disadvantaged backgrounds. The Brothers’ educational mission goes beyond academic excellence. It seeks the holistic formation of young people through discipline, hard work, and strong moral and spiritual values. Their approach aims to prepare youth for life by promoting maturity, scientific thinking, healthy competition, cooperation, and true sportsmanship. Equally important is nurturing sensitivity to the needs and rights of others—especially the poor—along with religious tolerance and a spirit of national integration.The congregation works collaboratively with like-minded organizations, governmental and non-governmental, to develop God-loving, responsible, and competent citizens. Their efforts form part of a broader vision of human resource development rooted in dignity, compassion, and service.
about-beyond-p1: While the congregation places great emphasis on formal schooling, it also invests significantly in technical education for young people. The Brothers are equally committed to social and community development, engaging in grassroots initiatives, social work, and advocacy for the upliftment of the poor, the marginalized, and the oppressed. These activities form an integral part of their Montfortian mission.

about-aim-p1: The aim of Gabrielite education is to prepare students for life by forming them into transformative leaders of competence, conscience, and compassion, committed to the service of their fellow human beings.
about-aim-p2: Inspired by St. Louis-Marie de Montfort, who lived by the motto “God Alone,” Gabrielite education seeks to help every learner become an integrated person by developing qualities of mind and heart, along with the necessary skills and attitudes that enable them to be concerned and contributing members of society and the nation.
about-char-sub: The Gabrielite system of education is distinguished by the following characteristics
about-char1-desc: Acknowledges God as the origin and goal of all life, guiding students to find meaning and purpose through faith expressed in service.
about-char2-desc: Recognizes each learner as unique and gifted, fostering holistic growth of mind, body, and spirit.
about-char3-desc: Promotes sensitivity to others, inclusivity, non-violence, peace, and justice.
about-char4-desc: Encourages competence, teamwork, innovation, and ethical responsibility.
about-char5-desc: Fosters responsible citizenship, loyalty to the Constitution, respect for rights, and appreciation of cultural heritage.
about-char6-title: Promoting Universal Brotherhood/Sisterhood and International Understanding
about-char6-desc: Cultivates empathy, solidarity, and intercultural dialogue.
about-char7-desc: Prioritizes service to the poor, marginalized, and vulnerable.
about-char8-desc: Promotes ecological awareness, sustainable living, and stewardship of creation.
about-char9-desc: Aims to form leaders who embody competence, conscience, and compassion, fostering harmony with self, others, creation, and God.

proj-idp-title: Construction of a Primary School Hostel, Kyebando, Mayuge
proj-idp-desc1: In rural Uganda, many children walk 5–10 km daily to attend school. Heavy rains and unsafe travel conditions lead to high dropout rates—especially among girls.
proj-idp-desc2: The Challenge: Long distances and unsafe commutes hindering education access.
proj-idp-mission-text: To construct a safe, 196-capacity hostel including dormitories, sanitation, and solar lighting to provide stability for vulnerable students.
proj-idp-desc-sub: This hostel is more than just a building; it is a shield for the future of Kyebando’s children, ensuring they stay in school regardless of the weather or distance.
